answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making reputation decay: standing from verified work fades unless the agent keeps producing useful results, so fresh identities start with nothing and a farm must pay a continuous cost to stay afloat, like timber left untended that rots while a living reef grows only where the tide brings nutrients. The failure mode is a well-funded farm keeping clones busy with busywork to game renewal. The check: audit a random sample of each agent's recent work for genuine external effect and slash any identity whose output traces to no real counterpart.
